operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The clause is the single command of the order: it amends Executive Order 10349 by striking out the date June 30, 1952 in the introductory paragraph and inserting July 3, 1952. That command is a one-time act completed when the President signed the order on 1952-06-30, the date printed under the signature; the order states no later effective date, and no condition or duration keeps the command itself operating afterwards. Recorded as exhausted by performance on that date. The consequence of the act, the substituted date in Executive Order 10349, is a separate surviving effect and is not claimed to have ended here. If the amendment were instead read as taking effect only on publication in the Federal Register on 1952-07-02, the end date would move to that day; the held text gives no basis for that reading.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10367 (17 FR 5929), signed by President Truman on 1952-06-30, is one paragraph. Its only command amends Executive Order 10349 of April 26, 1952 (as already amended by Executive Orders 10356 and 10362) by striking out one date, June 30, 1952, in the introductory paragraph of that order and inserting July 3, 1952 in its place. The held Federal Register text was read in full: heading, recital of authority, the amending command and the signature, with no duration, condition, report, delegation, savings sentence or second command. The command is a one-time amendment that is performed by issuing the order; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 it is recorded as exhausted by performance on the signing date, separately from its surviving consequence, which is that the substituted date stands in the text of Executive Order 10349, a different instrument whose own lifecycle this claim does not decide. The order states no effective date, so the amendment is treated as effective on signature. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) report no instrument that revoked, superseded or amended Executive Order 10367; the two catalog hits are cross-reference entries in the notes for Executive Orders 10356 and 10362 that point to this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The only operative sentence opens the returns to inspection by the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives or a duly authorized subcommittee until June 30, 1953. The stated until-date is the order's own end. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 it is recorded inclusive, 1953-06-30, meaning the permission runs through the end of that day; the exclusive reading, under which the permission ends when June 30, 1953 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. The permission is also tied to the Committee's inquiry authorized by its resolution of January 27, 1953, but no held source shows that the inquiry ended earlier, so the fixed date is the first end. No extension was found in the held corpus.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10451 of 1953-04-28 (18 FR 2529; Federal Register Document 53-3883, filed 1953-04-30) orders that, until June 30, 1953, specified federal tax returns for periods through 1952 are open to inspection by the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives or a duly authorized subcommittee, in connection with the inquiry authorized by its resolution of January 27, 1953 into the administration of the Department of Justice and the Office of the Attorney General, subject to the conditions in the Treasury decision approved the same date. The held Federal Register text file contains this order followed by unrelated Civil Service Commission rules and a contents page from the same issue; the dossier's eleven clauses (including scopes labelled Schedule C, items and 633) were generated from those neighbouring documents, so the inventory is corrected to the single operative paragraph of the order. The order is a time-limited permission whose own wording fixes its end, so the terminating event is the stated until-date. Per the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates the end is recorded inclusive as 1953-06-30 (the order runs through that day); the alternative exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins. No extension, amendment, revocation or supersession was found: the selected machine searches report none, and a search of all held order texts for the number 10451 and for inspection orders for this Committee finds only this order itself and orders for other committees or other periods.

The permission is tied to an inquiry, but nothing held shows that the inquiry or the Committee's use of the permission ended before June 30, 1953, and a deadline or condition is not treated as proof that an event occurred.","independent_command_check":"There is no independent command. The order contains one permission (inspection of the listed returns by the Committee) limited by the same sentence to the period ending June 30, 1953, and by the conditions of the Treasury decision it refers to. No delegation, reporting duty or standing rule is present.","savings_check":"The order has no savings sentence. The Treasury decision it incorporates is not an instrument held in this packet, and this claim makes no finding about it.","scope_check":"The dossier clauses other than the lead were produced from the Civil Service Commission Schedule C rules and the issue contents printed after the order on the same page, so they are not clauses of this order. The corrected inventory is one clause covering the single operative paragraph of the order, from the words beginning By virtue of the authority to the words ending approved by me this date (characters 772 to 1755 of the held text), which contains every operative word of the order."}

That command is a one-time act completed when the President signed the order on 1962-02-06, the date printed under the signature; the order states no later effective date and no condition or duration keeps the command operating afterwards. If the amendment were instead read as taking effect on publication in the Federal Register, the end date would move to the publication day; the held text gives no basis for that reading.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10991 of 1962-02-06 (Federal Register Document 62-1426, filed 1962-02-08) is one paragraph signed by President Kennedy. Its only command amends Executive Order 10929 of March 24, 1961, which provides for a commission to consider a controversy between the carriers represented by the New York Harbor Conference Carriers' Committee and certain of their employees, by substituting a new second sentence in section 1 of that order: the commission is to consist of nine members, three from persons nominated by the carriers, three from persons nominated by the employees, and the chairman and two other members without nominations. The held Federal Register text was read in full; it has no duration, condition, report, delegation or savings wording and no second command. The command is a one-time amendment performed by issuing the order; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 it is recorded as exhausted by performance on the signing date, separately from its surviving consequence, which is the substituted sentence in Executive Order 10929, a different instrument whose own lifecycle this claim does not decide. The order states no effective date, so the amendment is treated as effective on signature. The selected machine searches report no instrument that revoked, superseded or amended Executive Order 10991. Held order texts that name number 10929 were also checked and none acts on Executive Order 10991.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(1): the Administrator may exercise the President's authority under section 6(d) of the United States Housing Act of 1937 to approve the undertaking by the Public Housing Administration of annual contributions, grants or loans. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(2): the Administrator may exercise the President's authority under section 14 of the United States Housing Act of 1937 to approve the amending or superseding of contracts for annual contributions or loans so that the going Federal rate is that on the date of approval. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 14 of the 
United States Housing Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 895 (42 U.S.C. 1414), 
to approve the amendmg or superseding of any contract for annual 
contributions or loans, or both, so that the going Federal rate on the 
basis of which such annual contributions or the interest rate on the 
loans, or both, respectively, are fixed shall mean the going Federal 
rate on the date of approval of the amending or superseding contract 
entered into by the Public Housing Administration.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(3): the Administrator may exercise the authority of the Housing and Home Finance Administrator under section 103(b) of the Housing Act of 1949, with the President's approval otherwise required, to contract to make grants under Title I of that Act. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(4): the Administrator may exercise the President's authority under Title II of the Act of June 28, 1940 to determine that housing is no longer needed for national-defense dwellings, with the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
(4) The authority vested in the President by Title I I  of the Act of 
June 28, 1940, ch. 440, 54 Stat. 681 (42 U.S.C. 1501-1505), to deter­
mine that housing administered or assisted by the Public Housing 
Administration under that Title is no longer needed to assure the 
availability of dwellings for persons engaged in national-defense 
activities : Provided% That determinations under this paragraph shall 
require the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1(5): the Administrator may exercise the President's authority under section 5 of the Act of June 29, 1936 to approve dedication of streets, alleys and parks and the granting of easements in connection with low-cost housing or slum-clearance projects. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
(5) The authority vested in the President by Section 5 of the Act 
of June 29, 1936, ch. 860, 49 Stat. 2026, to approve the dedication by 
the Public Housing Commissioner of streets, alleys, and parks for 
public use, and the granting by the Commissioner of easements, in 
connection with any low-cost housing or slum-clearance project 
described in that Act.

Thursday , February 4, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER
Executive Order 11196
PROVIDING FOR THE PERFORMANCE BY THE HOUSING AND HOME
FINANCE ADMINISTRATOR OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS VESTED IN OR
SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows—
S ection  1. The Housing and Home Finance Administrator is 
hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, 
ratification, or other action of the President, the following:
(1) The authority vested in the President by Section 6(d) of the 
United States Housmg Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 888 (42 U.S.C. 1406(d) ), 
to approve the undertaking by the Public Housing Administration 
of any annual contribution, grant, or loan, or any contract for any 
annual contribution, grant, or loan, under that Act.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 14 of the 
United States Housing Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 895 (42 U.S.C. 1414), 
to approve the amendmg or superseding of any contract for annual 
contributions or loans, or both, so that the going Federal rate on the 
basis of which such annual contributions or the interest rate on the 
loans, or both, respectively, are fixed shall mean the going Federal 
rate on the date of approval of the amending or superseding contract 
entered into by the Public Housing Administration.
(3) The authority vested in the Housing and Home Finance Ad­
ministrator by Section 103(b) of the Housing Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 
416 (42 U.S.C. 1453(b) ), to contract, with the approval of the Presi­
dent, to make grants under Title I  of that Act.
(4) The authority vested in the President by Title I I  of the Act of 
June 28, 1940, ch. 440, 54 Stat. 681 (42 U.S.C. 1501-1505), to deter­
mine that housing administered or assisted by the Public Housing 
Administration under that Title is no longer needed to assure the 
availability of dwellings for persons engaged in national-defense 
activities : Provided% That determinations under this paragraph shall 
require the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.
(5) The authority vested in the President by Section 5 of the Act 
of June 29, 1936, ch. 860, 49 Stat. 2026, to approve the dedication by 
the Public Housing Commissioner of streets, alleys, and parks for 
public use, and the granting by the Commissioner of easements, in 
connection with any low-cost housing or slum-clearance project 
described in that Act.
(6) The authority vested in the President by Section 57 of the 
Alaska Omnibus Act (added by Public Law 88-451 of August 19, 
1964, 78 Stat. 507), (A) to make the grants to the State of Alaska 
provided for in that Section, (B) to approve a plan submitted by the 
State of Alaska for the implementation of the purpose of that Section,
(C) to specify reports to be made by the agency designated by the 
State of Alaska in accordance with that Section and to prescribe the 
form of, and information to be contained in, such reports, and (D) 
to demand access to the records upon which such reports are based.
S ec. 2. The following are hereby superseded :

added paragraph (g) to Section 4 of Executive Order No. 10530 of 
May 10, 1954.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2(1): Part III of Executive Order 10530 of May 10, 1954 is superseded. The command is a one-time act that was performed when the order issued; the order states no later effective date, so it is recorded as exhausted by performance on the signing date 1965-02-02 (filed that day, Federal Register issue of February 4, 1965). Executive Order 12553 later revoked Executive Order 11196 as a whole on 1986-02-25, recorded as a later event; this claim does not treat that revocation as reviving the superseded order. No earlier named instrument was found.

Thursday , February 4, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER
Executive Order 11196
PROVIDING FOR THE PERFORMANCE BY THE HOUSING AND HOME
FINANCE ADMINISTRATOR OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS VESTED IN OR
SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows—
S ection  1. The Housing and Home Finance Administrator is 
hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, 
ratification, or other action of the President, the following:
(1) The authority vested in the President by Section 6(d) of the 
United States Housmg Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 888 (42 U.S.C. 1406(d) ), 
to approve the undertaking by the Public Housing Administration 
of any annual contribution, grant, or loan, or any contract for any 
annual contribution, grant, or loan, under that Act.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 14 of the 
United States Housing Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 895 (42 U.S.C. 1414), 
to approve the amendmg or superseding of any contract for annual 
contributions or loans, or both, so that the going Federal rate on the 
basis of which such annual contributions or the interest rate on the 
loans, or both, respectively, are fixed shall mean the going Federal 
rate on the date of approval of the amending or superseding contract 
entered into by the Public Housing Administration.
(3) The authority vested in the Housing and Home Finance Ad­
ministrator by Section 103(b) of the Housing Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 
416 (42 U.S.C. 1453(b) ), to contract, with the approval of the Presi­
dent, to make grants under Title I  of that Act.
(4) The authority vested in the President by Title I I  of the Act of 
June 28, 1940, ch. 440, 54 Stat. 681 (42 U.S.C. 1501-1505), to deter­
mine that housing administered or assisted by the Public Housing 
Administration under that Title is no longer needed to assure the 
availability of dwellings for persons engaged in national-defense 
activities : Provided% That determinations under this paragraph shall 
require the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.
(5) The authority vested in the President by Section 5 of the Act 
of June 29, 1936, ch. 860, 49 Stat. 2026, to approve the dedication by 
the Public Housing Commissioner of streets, alleys, and parks for 
public use, and the granting by the Commissioner of easements, in 
connection with any low-cost housing or slum-clearance project 
described in that Act.
(6) The authority vested in the President by Section 57 of the 
Alaska Omnibus Act (added by Public Law 88-451 of August 19, 
1964, 78 Stat. 507), (A) to make the grants to the State of Alaska 
provided for in that Section, (B) to approve a plan submitted by the 
State of Alaska for the implementation of the purpose of that Section,
(C) to specify reports to be made by the agency designated by the 
State of Alaska in accordance with that Section and to prescribe the 
form of, and information to be contained in, such reports, and (D) 
to demand access to the records upon which such reports are based.
S ec. 2. The following are hereby superseded :
(1) P art I I I  of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10, 1954.
(2) Executive Order No. 10573 of October 26,1954.
(3) Executive Order No. 10852 of November 27, 1959.
(4) So much of Executive Order No. 11184 of October 13,1964, as 
added paragraph (g) to Section 4 of Executive Order No. 10530 of 
May 10, 1954.
■  Sec. 3. (a) References in this Order to any statute or to any provi­
sion of any statute shall be deemed to include (1) to the extent not 
inappropriate, references thereto as amended from time to time, (2) 
in the cases of Sections 1(1), 1(2), 1(4), and 1(5) of this Order, ref­
erences to Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1947 (61 Stat. 954), and (3)

=== PDF page 8 of 72 ===
1172 THE PRESIDENT
in the case of Section 1(5) of this Order, a reference to Executive 
Order No. 7732 of October 27,1937.
(b) Unless inappropriate, any reference in any Executive order 
to any Executive order which is superseded by this Order, or to any 
Executive order provision so superseded, shall hereafter be deemed 
to refer to this Order or to the provision of Section 1 hereof, if any, 
which corresponds to the superseded provision.
S ec. A. All actions heretofore taken by the President or by his dele­
gate in respect of the matters affected by Section 1 of this Order and 
in force at the time of the issuance of this Order shall, except as they 
may be inconsistent with the provisions of this Order, remain in effect 
until amended, modified, or revoked pursuant to the authority con­
ferred by this Order unless sooner terminated by operation of law.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2(2): Executive Order 10573 of October 26, 1954 is superseded. The command is a one-time act that was performed when the order issued; the order states no later effective date, so it is recorded as exhausted by performance on the signing date 1965-02-02 (filed that day, Federal Register issue of February 4, 1965). Executive Order 12553 later revoked Executive Order 11196 as a whole on 1986-02-25, recorded as a later event; this claim does not treat that revocation as reviving the superseded order. No earlier named instrument was found.

Thursday , February 4, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER
Executive Order 11196
PROVIDING FOR THE PERFORMANCE BY THE HOUSING AND HOME
FINANCE ADMINISTRATOR OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS VESTED IN OR
SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows—
S ection  1. The Housing and Home Finance Administrator is 
hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, 
ratification, or other action of the President, the following:
(1) The authority vested in the President by Section 6(d) of the 
United States Housmg Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 888 (42 U.S.C. 1406(d) ), 
to approve the undertaking by the Public Housing Administration 
of any annual contribution, grant, or loan, or any contract for any 
annual contribution, grant, or loan, under that Act.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 14 of the 
United States Housing Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 895 (42 U.S.C. 1414), 
to approve the amendmg or superseding of any contract for annual 
contributions or loans, or both, so that the going Federal rate on the 
basis of which such annual contributions or the interest rate on the 
loans, or both, respectively, are fixed shall mean the going Federal 
rate on the date of approval of the amending or superseding contract 
entered into by the Public Housing Administration.
(3) The authority vested in the Housing and Home Finance Ad­
ministrator by Section 103(b) of the Housing Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 
416 (42 U.S.C. 1453(b) ), to contract, with the approval of the Presi­
dent, to make grants under Title I  of that Act.
(4) The authority vested in the President by Title I I  of the Act of 
June 28, 1940, ch. 440, 54 Stat. 681 (42 U.S.C. 1501-1505), to deter­
mine that housing administered or assisted by the Public Housing 
Administration under that Title is no longer needed to assure the 
availability of dwellings for persons engaged in national-defense 
activities : Provided% That determinations under this paragraph shall 
require the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.
(5) The authority vested in the President by Section 5 of the Act 
of June 29, 1936, ch. 860, 49 Stat. 2026, to approve the dedication by 
the Public Housing Commissioner of streets, alleys, and parks for 
public use, and the granting by the Commissioner of easements, in 
connection with any low-cost housing or slum-clearance project 
described in that Act.
(6) The authority vested in the President by Section 57 of the 
Alaska Omnibus Act (added by Public Law 88-451 of August 19, 
1964, 78 Stat. 507), (A) to make the grants to the State of Alaska 
provided for in that Section, (B) to approve a plan submitted by the 
State of Alaska for the implementation of the purpose of that Section,
(C) to specify reports to be made by the agency designated by the 
State of Alaska in accordance with that Section and to prescribe the 
form of, and information to be contained in, such reports, and (D) 
to demand access to the records upon which such reports are based.
S ec. 2. The following are hereby superseded :
(1) P art I I I  of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10, 1954.
(2) Executive Order No. 10573 of October 26,1954.
(3) Executive Order No. 10852 of November 27, 1959.
(4) So much of Executive Order No. 11184 of October 13,1964, as 
added paragraph (g) to Section 4 of Executive Order No. 10530 of 
May 10, 1954.

erences to Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1947 (61 Stat. 954), and (3)

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2(3): Executive Order 10852 of November 27, 1959 is superseded. The command is a one-time act that was performed when the order issued; the order states no later effective date, so it is recorded as exhausted by performance on the signing date 1965-02-02 (filed that day, Federal Register issue of February 4, 1965). Executive Order 12553 later revoked Executive Order 11196 as a whole on 1986-02-25, recorded as a later event; this claim does not treat that revocation as reviving the superseded order. No earlier named instrument was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3(b) and section 4: references in other orders to superseded orders are deemed references to this order, and prior actions on the covered matters remain in effect until amended, modified or revoked pursuant to the authority conferred, unless sooner terminated by operation of law. Ended by the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237). The order revokes the listed Executive Orders and any amendments thereto and states no effective date other than signature, so the signing date is used. No earlier named instrument was found; later HUD delegation notices that mention the order are counterevidence considered and not accepted (see the research rationale).

Thursday , February 4, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER
Executive Order 11196
PROVIDING FOR THE PERFORMANCE BY THE HOUSING AND HOME
FINANCE ADMINISTRATOR OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS VESTED IN OR
SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows—
S ection  1. The Housing and Home Finance Administrator is 
hereby designated and empowered to exercise, without the approval, 
ratification, or other action of the President, the following:
(1) The authority vested in the President by Section 6(d) of the 
United States Housmg Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 888 (42 U.S.C. 1406(d) ), 
to approve the undertaking by the Public Housing Administration 
of any annual contribution, grant, or loan, or any contract for any 
annual contribution, grant, or loan, under that Act.
(2) The authority vested in the President by Section 14 of the 
United States Housing Act of 1937, 50 Stat. 895 (42 U.S.C. 1414), 
to approve the amendmg or superseding of any contract for annual 
contributions or loans, or both, so that the going Federal rate on the 
basis of which such annual contributions or the interest rate on the 
loans, or both, respectively, are fixed shall mean the going Federal 
rate on the date of approval of the amending or superseding contract 
entered into by the Public Housing Administration.
(3) The authority vested in the Housing and Home Finance Ad­
ministrator by Section 103(b) of the Housing Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 
416 (42 U.S.C. 1453(b) ), to contract, with the approval of the Presi­
dent, to make grants under Title I  of that Act.
(4) The authority vested in the President by Title I I  of the Act of 
June 28, 1940, ch. 440, 54 Stat. 681 (42 U.S.C. 1501-1505), to deter­
mine that housing administered or assisted by the Public Housing 
Administration under that Title is no longer needed to assure the 
availability of dwellings for persons engaged in national-defense 
activities : Provided% That determinations under this paragraph shall 
require the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.
(5) The authority vested in the President by Section 5 of the Act 
of June 29, 1936, ch. 860, 49 Stat. 2026, to approve the dedication by 
the Public Housing Commissioner of streets, alleys, and parks for 
public use, and the granting by the Commissioner of easements, in 
connection with any low-cost housing or slum-clearance project 
described in that Act.
(6) The authority vested in the President by Section 57 of the 
Alaska Omnibus Act (added by Public Law 88-451 of August 19, 
1964, 78 Stat. 507), (A) to make the grants to the State of Alaska 
provided for in that Section, (B) to approve a plan submitted by the 
State of Alaska for the implementation of the purpose of that Section,
(C) to specify reports to be made by the agency designated by the 
State of Alaska in accordance with that Section and to prescribe the 
form of, and information to be contained in, such reports, and (D) 
to demand access to the records upon which such reports are based.
S ec. 2. The following are hereby superseded :
(1) P art I I I  of Executive Order No. 10530 of May 10, 1954.
(2) Executive Order No. 10573 of October 26,1954.
(3) Executive Order No. 10852 of November 27, 1959.
(4) So much of Executive Order No. 11184 of October 13,1964, as 
added paragraph (g) to Section 4 of Executive Order No. 10530 of 
May 10, 1954.

sion of any statute shall be deemed to include (1) to the extent not 
inappropriate, references thereto as amended from time to time, (2) 
in the cases of Sections 1(1), 1(2), 1(4), and 1(5) of this Order, ref­
erences to Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1947 (61 Stat. 954), and (3)

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11196 (30 FR 1171; Federal Register Document 65-1259, filed 1965-02-02), signed by President Johnson, designates the Housing and Home Finance Administrator to exercise without presidential approval six listed statutory functions (section 1), supersedes four earlier orders or order parts (section 2), states two rules of construction (section 3) and preserves prior actions (section 4). The held text is the Federal Register page text; its OCR misprints the signature year as 1966, while the filing note, the Federal Register issue date (February 4, 1965) and the dossier signing date give February 1965. The dossier's twelve clause spans cover the order without gap; they are read as: preamble and section 1 lead, section 1(1) to (6), section 2(1) to (4), section 3(a), and section 3(b) with section 4. Nine clauses (the preamble and section 1 lead, section 1(1) to (6), section 2(4) with section 3(a), and section 3(b) with section 4) ended with the express revocation of Executive Order 11196 by number in the revocation table of Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237), which revokes the listed orders and any amendments thereto and states no later effective date. The three one-time supersessions in section 2(1) to (3) are recorded, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 on exhaustion by performance, as exhausted on the signing date 1965-02-02, with the 1986 revocation as a later event. Two held Department of Housing and Urban Development delegation notices of 2006 and 2015, surfaced by Selden, still describe an authority delegated under Executive Order 11196; they are delegations by the Secretary (71 FR 60169, published 2006-10-12; 80 FR 21756, published 2015-04-20) under section 7(d) of the HUD Act, cannot restore a presidential order revoked in 1986, and are recorded as counterevidence considered and not accepted. The Selden statute excerpts (49 Stat. 2026, 50 Stat. 888 and 895, 63 Stat. 416, 78 Stat. 507) are the statutes the order cites; none was read as ending the order, since the order is a delegation resting on them and no held text shows their repeal. The selected machine searches report U.S. Code notes that record this order as revoked by Executive Order 12553; the packet holds those notes only as pointers.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The first instrument that names Executive Order 11196 and ends it is Executive Order 12553 (1986-02-25). Statutes that rewrote the housing programs after 1965 (the dossier flags Public Law 89-174 and Public Law 93-383, neither held as text here) do not name this order, so under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments they are disclosed as possible earlier candidate ends rather than as ends; no held text shows that either extinguished a specific command of this order.","independent_command_check":"The six delegations in section 1 are independent commands, but each is a delegation to the same officer under the same order and ended together with the order by the revocation by number. Sections 3 and 4 depend on the order and ended with it. No command outlives the revocation inside the order's text.","savings_check":"Section 4 of the order preserved prior presidential or delegate actions on the covered matters unless sooner terminated by operation of law. Executive Order 12553 contains no sentence preserving or undoing prior actions (read in full). Completed approvals under section 1 are accrued acts. The functions themselves rest on the statutes the order cites, and this claim makes no finding about who exercises them after 1986. The 2006 and 2015 HUD notices do not establish a continuing presidential delegation.","scope_check":"The twelve clause spans run without gap from the preamble to the end of section 4. Section 1 has one lead and six delegated authorities; section 2 supersedes four earlier orders or parts by number; section 3 and section 4 state references and preserve prior actions. The nine continuing or standing clauses share the single ending instrument, Executive Order 12553. The three clauses that only supersede named earlier orders (section 2(1) to (3)) are one-time acts performed on issuance, so their first end is the signing date and the 1986 revocation is a later event on them; this follows the same exhaustion-by-performance reading applied to the amending orders in this batch."}

savings_residuals.reason: Section 4 of Executive Order 11196 continued earlier actions on the covered matters; completed approvals under section 1 are accrued acts that the 1986 revocation does not itself undo, because Executive Order 12553 contains no sentence undoing prior actions. The statutory functions the order delegated remain with whoever the statutes name, which this claim does not decide; no continuing presidential delegation is shown by any held text.
